text: Good manufacturing practice (GMP) helps ensure products are consistently produced and controlled to quality standards. Manufacturing processes and important changes should be documented.
Pharmaceutical quality control includes sampling, testing, and review of materials and products against approved specifications before release.
Pharmacovigilance involves detecting, assessing, understanding, and preventing adverse effects and other medicine-related problems.
Clinical trials involving human participants require an approved protocol, informed consent, appropriate oversight, and review by an ethics committee or institutional review board.
Batch records and distribution records help organizations trace materials and products through manufacturing and the supply chain.
A regulatory submission organizes evidence about a product's quality, safety, and efficacy for review by the relevant health authority.
